messages:
maria: Heads-up — after the rate-limit policy push at 18:04 UTC a few customers are seeing 429 spikes. Canary was green but we're getting cluster-level rejects now :eyes:

devon: Which policy id and rollout percent?

maria: policy_id=rl-2024-08-15, rolled to 30% prod via rollout service. snippet from the push log:
```json
{
  "policy_id": "rl-2024-08-15",
  "changes": { "global_qps": 1200, "burst_window_ms": 1000 },
  "percent": 30
}
```

anya: Seeing rise in `reject_count` on rate-metrics (redis counter) starting ~18:10 UTC. Also prefix cache miss rate jumped ~3x for tokens from partner X. Might be a concentrated burst pattern not covered by the new smoothing window.

sre-bot: ALERT: rate-limit-policy-rollout - policy=rl-2024-08-15 severity=warning replicaset=prod-eu rejects=1120 5m

luke: Can we narrow the rollout or revert? Options: pause rollout, set percent->10, or rollback to previous policy. I can run a rollback if we want immediate mitigation.

devon: Before rollback — can we repro quickly? Maria, do you have a request sample + headers that produced 429? We should confirm it is policy and not auth throttle.

maria: sample payload (sanitized) + response snippet:
```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \\n  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED" \\n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\n  -d '{"input":"long sequence repeated to hit token route","max_tokens":1024}' \\n  -w "\nHTTP:%{http_code}\n"
```
response: `{"error":"rate_limit_exceeded","retry_after":2}` HTTP:429

anya: Confirmed in infra logs: token-bucket reject path hit the trajectory we expected when burst_window_ms lowered. Partner X sent high-frequency short requests that bypassed our client-side batching.

billing-bot: FYI — 3 accounts that got 429s also triggered billing-protection flags (safety hold) — CS is engaged to avoid invoice-affecting churn.

luke: I'm going to do a staged rollback to 10% for prod-eu + prod-na to reduce surface area. Command I'll run:```
redwoodctl rollout set --policy rl-2024-08-15 --percent 10 --env prod --regions eu,na
```
If that doesn't stabilize, I'll cancel rollout:```
redwoodctl rollout cancel --policy rl-2024-08-15 --env prod
```

maria: +1 do the 10% first. I'll ping CS and affected customers explaining temporary throughput impact and recommend client retry/backoff (exponential with jitter).

devon: After Luke reduces percent, I'll tail the reject counters and KV cache miss graphs. If rejects fall back to baseline, we'll keep 10% and run a narrower canary focusing on partner traffic only.

anya: Quick repro script for infra if needed (run from staging to simulate):
```bash
for i in {1..500}; do \\
  curl -s -X POST https://staging.api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer test" -d '{"input":"x"}' &\\
  sleep 0.01\ndone
```
This reproduces bursty small requests and hits threshold within ~10s.

maria: Customer mitigation notes I sent to CS thread: 1) reduce per-request token size 2) implement jittered retry (start=250ms, max=4s) 3) queue/batch outbound requests on client side 4) reach out if seeing >10% error rate.

luke: Rollout set ->10% executed at 18:23 UTC. Monitoring now. :thumbsup:

sre-bot: INFO: rollout-update policy=rl-2024-08-15 percent=10 regions=eu,na timestamp=2402110200

devon: Early signal — reject_rate dropped ~65% in eu within 2m. KV misses still slightly elevated, watching for rebound.

billing-bot: Billing holds cleared for 2 of 3 accounts after transient retries; CS is following up on the third.

maria: Thanks all. Action items:
- luke: keep rollout at 10% for 30m, then either continue canary with partner-scoped rule or cancel.
- devon: validate metrics + set alert to watch `reject_count` and `prefix_miss_rate`.
- anya: investigate whether smoothing window should be increased or add partner-specific exception.
- CS: inform affected customers and share retry guidance (maria).

Please react to confirm ownership :raised_hands:
